title: A pre-rasterised PNG vs the SVG it was rendered from, held static
variable: PNG texture vs SVG source, same picture, no churn
claim: The control half of the SVG-vs-PNG question raised by the FilterableDataTable pagination finding, where swapping 23 flag SVGs for PNGs removed a visible per-click spike. That observation was made inside a Solid.js app, so the format was never isolated. This case asks the narrow question the churn cases need answered first: with the element set fixed and only the shared damage driver running, does an SVG cost more per frame than the PNG rasterised from it? A null here says vector artwork is rasterised once and reused, which makes any cost the churn cases find a cost of element creation rather than of the format as such. A positive here says the SVG is re-rasterised on frames that redraw it, which would be a much larger finding than the pagination spike suggested.
result: Confirmed on the hypothesized axis (Paint), but small: 1.73x at 30, 1.87x at 100, 2.81x at 300, with Styles and Layout flat throughout and GPU moving only at 300 (1.62x). The absolute cost is sub-millisecond in both variants (Paint 0.28ms vs 0.78ms at 300), so this is a real but minor per-frame charge. What matters is what it rules out: cohtml does NOT fully bake the vector into a plain texture - there is residual per-frame work - but that residue is not what makes SVG expensive. Read against png-vs-svg-churn-complex: static 2.81x versus churn 462x at the same count says the cost is overwhelmingly paid at ELEMENT CREATION, not per frame. LIMITS: every tile shares one texture URL; measured on cohtml 3.1.2.1 while the rest of results.md is 3.2.0.2. COLD LOAD, measured separately and NOT a row in results.md: the initial build of a screen pays the same rasterisation this case only sees a residue of. Launching the Player on a blank page, starting the trace and only then navigating (cold-load-probe.mjs, which run.js cannot do - it discards 2s of warmup) gives a peak frame at 300 tiles of 1.12ms Paint for the PNG against 977.09ms for the SVG, and 92.04ms for a 4-shape sprite. So a screen of 300 complex SVG tiles costs a single frozen frame of ~0.95s on load. Note the phase: cold load bills Paint and RecordRendering with Styles roughly flat, while churn bills Styles - the same work landing in a different phase depending on whether elements are built in one batch before first paint or re-resolved every frame. That last reading is inference from where the time lands, not verified engine behaviour. These numbers are PEAK frame, not the median results.md reports, which is why they are recorded here and in the probe rather than as a row.
notes: Applicability gate: DIRECT. background-image is listed partial in ../gameface-unsupported-features/results/css/partial.json, but only for element/gradients/image-rect/image-set values; url() is unaffected and was already exercised by image-oversized-vs-sized and many-images-vs-spritesheet. SVG as a url() source is not in the ../gameface-unsupported-features inventory either way, and it is the one thing that MUST be confirmed in the Player before a row from this case is trusted: if cohtml silently drops an SVG background, B renders empty tiles and the lab reports SVG as dramatically FASTER - a confident, inverted result. VERIFIED on Player 3.1.2.1: B.html renders 30 tiles at 88x64 with getComputedStyle reporting url(sprite.svg), and a screenshot shows the sprite drawn and matching A.html's. Re-check this on any engine version this case is re-run against. Rule 1: one variable, the asset format. Rule 2: identical DOM, identical geometry, identical background-size, so both variants render the same 88x64 picture in the same place. Rule 3: identical JS, byte-for-byte. Rule 4 EXCEPTION: the two variants load different assets - that IS the variable. tools/make-svg-cases.js rasterises sprite.png from sprite.svg itself, via @resvg/resvg-js, so the two are the same picture by construction rather than by two drawing routines agreeing. The one residual difference is inherent to the comparison and cannot be removed: at 88x64 the PNG has thrown away detail the SVG still carries, which is exactly what shipping a pre-rasterised asset means. Rule 5: 300 tiles occupy 1852x1032 inside 1920x1080. Rule 6: the shared root-nudge damage driver, identical in both - this case is the static control, so it deliberately does NOT churn. Rule 7: no randomness at runtime; the sprite generator is seeded, so regenerating the assets reproduces them byte-for-byte. Rule 8: counts 30/100/300. Rule 9: plain HTML/CSS/JS. Rule 10: expected axis is Paint - if the vector is re-rasterised per redraw it should be billed where the tile is drawn. LIMIT: every tile shares one texture URL, which is the most favourable case for any raster cache the engine keeps. A null therefore does not clear SVG when a screen holds many DISTINCT vector assets; svg-distinct-vs-shared would be the case for that.
